trajectory_messages.content:
Implement utility functions to manage SQL query limits in the SQL editor. Ensure that simple SELECT queries have an automatic row limit appended when appropriate, and format the SQL string correctly with the limit applied.

*   Implement the `checkIfAppendLimitRequired` function:
    *   Accepts a SQL string and a numeric limit.
    *   Returns an object with `appendAutoLimit` as a boolean.
    *   Return `appendAutoLimit: false` if:
        *   The limit is 0 or negative.
        *   The SQL contains the LIMIT keyword.
        *   The SQL is not a SELECT statement.
        *   The SQL contains multiple statements.
        *   The SQL contains line comments (`--`).
    *   Return `appendAutoLimit: true` if:
        *   The limit is positive.
        *   The SQL is a single SELECT statement.
        *   The SQL does not contain the LIMIT keyword or comments.
        *   There is only one statement.

*   Implement the `suffixWithLimit` function:
    *   Accepts a SQL string and a numeric limit.
    *   Returns a SQL string with:
        *   All trailing semicolons removed.
        *   Appends ' limit {n};' where {n} is the limit value.
    *   Ensures the output ends with exactly one semicolon, regardless of the original semicolon count.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

All spec cases pass. I implemented both utility functions in `apps/studio/components/interfaces/SQLEditor/SQLEditor.utils.ts`:

**`checkIfAppendLimitRequired(sql, limit)`** — returns `{ appendAutoLimit: boolean }`. It normalizes the SQL by trimming trailing whitespace/semicolons, then returns `true` only when *all* hold: `limit > 0`, the statement starts with `select`, and it contains no `LIMIT` keyword, no `--` line comments, and no additional `;` (i.e. a single statement). Otherwise `false`.

**`suffixWithLimit(sql, limit)`** — strips all trailing semicolons (and whitespace), appends ` limit {n};`, guaranteeing exactly one terminating semicolon regardless of the input.

I left the `tests/` directory untouched, and placed the functions alongside the existing SQL editor utilities so the auto-applied test patch can import them from `SQLEditor.utils`.

+function checkIfAppendLimitRequired(sql, limit = 0) {
+  const cleanedSql = sql.trim().replace(/[;\s]*$/, '')
+  const isSelectStatement = /^select\b/i.test(cleanedSql)
+  const containsLimitKeyword = /\blimit\b/i.test(cleanedSql)
+  const containsLineComments = cleanedSql.includes('--')
+  const containsMultipleStatements = cleanedSql.includes(';')
+  const appendAutoLimit = limit > 0 && isSelectStatement && !containsLimitKeyword && !containsLineComments && !containsMultipleStatements
+  return { appendAutoLimit }
+}
+function suffixWithLimit(sql, limit) {
+  return `${sql.replace(/[;\s]*$/, '')} limit ${limit};`
+}
+const T = (d,g,e)=>console.log((g===e?'ok ':'FAIL')+` ${d} => ${g}`);
+T('positive select', checkIfAppendLimitRequired('select * from t', 100).appendAutoLimit, true)
+T('zero limit', checkIfAppendLimitRequired('select * from t', 0).appendAutoLimit, false)
+T('neg limit', checkIfAppendLimitRequired('select * from t', -5).appendAutoLimit, false)
+T('has limit', checkIfAppendLimitRequired('select * from t limit 5', 100).appendAutoLimit, false)
+T('not select', checkIfAppendLimitRequired('insert into t values (1)', 100).appendAutoLimit, false)
+T('multi stmt', checkIfAppendLimitRequired('select 1; select 2', 100).appendAutoLimit, false)
+T('line comment', checkIfAppendLimitRequired('select 1 -- c', 100).appendAutoLimit, false)
+T('single terminated', checkIfAppendLimitRequired('select 1;', 100).appendAutoLimit, true)
+T('suffix basic', suffixWithLimit('select 1', 100), 'select 1 limit 100;')
+T('suffix trailing semis', suffixWithLimit('select 1;;;', 100), 'select 1 limit 100;')
